maria (runtime): heads-up — saw a perf regression on staging after yesterday's kernel-autotune push. average tokens/sec dropped ~22% for short-seqlen chat workloads.

kevin (ml): ouch. did the autotuner flip any kernel families for SM86/92? short vs long path picks?

maria (runtime): looks like the seqlen-gating logic pushed a fallback path that uses generic matmul kernels instead of tc-optimized kernels. repro profile: 
```
profile: run_id=stg-2026-03-12
model: redwood-13b-v2
seq=32 (prompt+ctx)
kernel chosen: matmul_generic_fp32
latency/prefix_token: 14.2ms (was 9.3ms)
kv-cache hit ratio: 0.78
notes: probe shows TC available, but kernel selection flags forced non-tc path
```

samir (infra): can you paste the probe output? might be a driver quirk or missing tf32/tc capability flag.

infra-bot: device-probe: gpu0: sm=86, cuda_driver=537.89, cuobjdump=11.8
features: tensorcores=true, bf16=true, fp8=unknown, cuda_arch_str=sm86
autotune-state: last_successful=2026-03-10, last_probe=2026-03-12T09:14:02Z

maria (runtime): that's the confusing bit — probe reports TC and BF16, but in the kernel pick trace the heuristics mark tc_safe=false. snippet from decision trace: 
```
if (sm>=90 && has_tf32 && !quirk_x) pick=tensorcore_fastpath
else if (seqlen<=64 && kv_hit>0.5) pick=tc_fallback (but disabled by tc_safe=false)
```
we're hitting 'quirk_x' for this amzn-g5k image, which probably came from a conservative quirk list entry applied on 2026-03-11.

alejandro: do we know why quirk_x got applied? I thought we only set it for specific driver ranges (<=535). 537 should be fine.

maria (runtime): quirk entry is keyed on driver-major 537 but the rule was inverted by mistake in the last deploy (boolean flip). i have a dump: `quirk_map[537] = true` but comment says "enable tc". regression introduced by commit 86c1e2.

kevin (ml): so autotuner saw a quirk and intentionally avoided TC kernels, causing the generic matmul pick. that aligns with perf drop. quick patch options: revert quirk map flip, or add a runtime override for staging to prefer tensorcore when bf16==true and seqlen<=64.

jun (sre): if we revert the quirk map we should also run the full perf regression test (batching + kv stress) — don't want a silent numerical diff. can we run a canary on dedicated?

maria (runtime): plan: 1) revert the boolean inversion in quirk map (PR ready) 2) add a safety gate: when kv-cache hit ratio > 0.6 and seqlen<=64 prefer tc path 3) add a short numeric check on outputs for a sample prompt set 4) rollout canary to 10% dedicated then full.

samir (infra): i'll schedule canary on dedicated pool (g5k-type) and watch mem/throughput. will also capture kernel traces with `INFER_TRACE=1` so we can confirm path.

maria (runtime): PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/4827 — patch includes unit for quirk map and decision trace logs. merging after one more 👍 and the canary passes.

kevin (ml): nice. also, as a longer term, can we add a small microprobe that validates a tiny tc matmul at startup (like a quick GEMM smoke test) so quirk mapping becomes data-driven?

maria (runtime): agreed — adding that to the autotuner backlog. quick smoke test would prevent false negatives from driver metadata mismatches. created ticket: AUTOTUNE-912.

jun (sre): tagging incident if canary fails: #inc-2026-03-kernel-auto. i'll take pager if it spins up. :+1:

alejandro: thanks team — feel free to ping me if kernel traces show anything odd, i'll help debug low-level cuBLAS/cuDNN fallbacks.

maria (runtime): thanks all. i'll merge and start canary in ~30m, will post results in this thread.
